articles.title: Leeds vs Newcastle: Daniel Farke sets out blueprint for success after unbeaten Premier League start
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview with Sky Sports, Daniel Farke explains his desire to take Leeds to new heights and reestablish his side as a Premier League staple; watch Leeds vs Newcastle live on Sky Sports Football on Monday; kick-off 8pm
articles.body:
From the early knockings, it's clear Farke is sticking with his tried and tested formula. A way of working that brought Leeds 47 points and had them in the comfort of safety by April last season.

"It's important to use momentum in the right way," he tells Sky Sports from Leeds' training base. "We needed to freshen blood after a successful season but it's about evolution not revolution". The blueprint is similar with subtle changes: Carry all the good things from the last campaign into this one but do so with added tactical variety.

He wants to keep Newcastle, or any opponent for that matter, guessing before, during and after the game. That is part of the reason why no player in Farke's squad is deemed undroppable. Not even his captain. When pushed on that topic, he says: "It's realistic. You always have to deliver in the best league in the world.

"If you think at any time 'I don't have to do the basics, I'm a superstar' then you are not good enough any more. I'm a big believer in you get what you are willing to invest.

"But if you know yourself to be doing one step less, or working with just 98 per cent, you are not good enough. The culture is more important than any individual. Of course we have outstanding individuals, they have good chances to play every week, but every player has to show the best of themselves every day."

The culture that Farke speaks of is geared toward establishing Leeds as a Premier League mainstay. "We're not addicted to one point per game," he emphasises, another distinction between last season and this. A point-per-game average used to be the yardstick by which Farke measured survival. They are more than just survivors now.

Adaptability is his new watchword. That might mean Leeds fall on the wrong side of certain results while trying to push for more wins, but the risk will be managed. Some demons have already been exorcised away at Nottingham Forest and Brighton, grounds they lost heavily at last year. "We're working on being less predictable. It can be fun, too.

"The DNA has not changed. We want to develop as a team, playing on the front foot with an offensive mind, even against the better teams. The work has been on our tactical flexibility. Now we can change the base formation, so we're not easy to predict."

Farke implemented a tactical tweak that altered the course of last season, switching from a back four to a back three. Extrinsically, it's a shift that was spoken about as a turning point. It followed a groundswell of pressure and unrest around Farke's position. Leeds responded by beating Chelsea and drawing with Liverpool, amid a run that landed them comfortably 14th.

The success of that streak drew praise from Jamie Carragher on Monday Night Football back in May: "I feel like I'm watching an established Premier League team."

Taking greater control in games was another reason for the system switch. "We are preparing a structure in possession for a moment if we lose the ball. The better we are in possession the easier it is to be spot on against the ball, to control the moments the opponent are dangerous.

"We want to have a good structure and be solid in possession." Summer additions James Trafford and Tarik Muharemovic have aided solidity immensely. The aura of confidence radiates from them throughout the spine of the team.

He adds: "The heart of our game has to be control, being stable is very important. It's up to this group to prove we are in a better position than last season, after three games I'm not willing to judge it. It's too early to sing high praises, but we've delivered some quality work in the last month. We have to ride with this moment."

Farke has earned the right to enter games with the aim of being the dominant force. Leeds have only lost one of their last 12 league outings since mid-March. And they thrive at Elland Road. He wants to see a "return to clinical behaviour" against Newcastle, after squandering chances to win at Brighton last week. But no doubt Leeds are harder to beat.

The level has been raised. "In the last 25 years, this club has never managed to play two solid Premier League seasons in a row. I want to do that," he concludes. Early days, but Leeds currently find themselves 11th.

"We are not praying for one point per game. We concentrate on the contents. One day to talk about Europe, to reestablish 'the good old times', would be nice. But we cannot take it for granted. I will make sure we are doing steps in the right direction and then, one day, we will speak about other goals.

"To win the Premier League? I would never say no. But I'm not addicted to the table. I'm addicted to performances and results. That is how it should look."

Watch Leeds vs Newcastle live on Sky Sports Football on Monday evening from 6.30pm; kick-off 8pm

articles.title: The ultimate Lane Kiffin what-if: Did he leave Ole Miss just before it reaches the pinnacle he's been chasing?
articles.summary: Kiffin left for LSU to chase championships. But with Trinidad Chambliss leading Ole Miss, he may have had his best shot by staying in Oxford. Did he bet on t...
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin has said many things over the last 15 years about his controversial exit from Tennessee to Southern Cal. But the one thing that has remained consistent is his lack of regret, even though the alternate history where he stays at Tennessee longer than one season almost certainly turns out better than his crash-and-burn in Los Angeles.

"I can't for the rest of my life watch USC on TV and go, 'I turned down that job,'" Kiffin told Sports Illustrated in 2016. "What would it have been like?"

There is little doubt the same what-if impulses drove Kiffin's mindset last season at Ole Miss as the coaching carousel started moving. Intoxicated with the idea of either becoming the second coming of Steve Spurrier at Florida or taking over an LSU program where significantly less talented coaches had won national titles, Kiffin was wired to look at the college football world through the same lens that drove him to USC after 2009.

It was simply not in Kiffin's nature to stay.

But as the fog has lifted since Saturday night, when Kiffin's return to Oxford, Mississippi, produced an epic 32-24 win for Pete Golding-led Ole Miss , we can see things a little more clearly.

There's a good chance Kiffin bet on the wrong horse for the same reason.

As Kiffin deliberated over his exit, his mind was surely consumed with the thought of watching someone else coach LSU to a national title and thinking it should have been him.

He likely never contemplated what it would be like in the opposite direction: What if Kiffin has to watch Trinidad Chambliss and Golding, two people he brought to Ole Miss, lift a trophy he may never win himself?

Kiffin is an elite evaluator of talent, but he's not the best evaluator of situations.

When Kiffin left Tennessee, he did not realize that USC was a different job during the Pete Carroll heyday he remembered. NCAA sanctions were coming, the school's leadership was fraying and recruiting trends were moving away from West Coast schools toward the SEC, which was about to embark on a generational run of championships.

And when Kiffin accepted the LSU job last December and was banished from the Ole Miss facility, he did not account for the possibility that he already had a national championship-caliber team on his hands or that Ole Miss would return in 2026 with the best quarterback in college football and a better chance than LSU to win the title this season.

If Kiffin could have foreseen all that last fall, would he still have left? He would, of course, say yes. But as infrequently as a job with LSU's mystique comes open, a team like the one Kiffin could have had at Ole Miss in 2026 is even more rare.

Maybe it will all work out for Kiffin in the end. With the resources LSU is devoting to football and the all-in support of Gov. Jeff Landry, who seems like the de facto athletic director these days, they are set up to be good for years to come.

But winning a national title is so hard. Everything has to go right, particularly in this 12-team playoff era. And with the universe of teams that can win a championship expanding beyond the traditional powers, Kiffin is at least as likely not to win one at LSU as he is to win one.

Traditionally, yes, LSU is a better bet than Ole Miss. Kiffin is not the first coach who has looked at LSU and thought, "If Ed Orgeron and Les Miles can win national titles there, imagine what I could do."

But the sport doesn't operate the same way now. Ole Miss, like many of the new-age contenders, has big money to spend, as well, and will continue to chip away at the historic ability of the blue-blood programs to stack up an insurmountable depth of talent.

More than ever, you have to catch lightning in the bottle. It is part tragedy, part comedy that Kiffin had already captured some in Chambliss, a former Division II quarterback who was so overlooked in the transfer portal that Kiffin's main competition was Temple .

Now look at him: The Heisman frontrunner (if there is such a thing after three weeks) for a team that already has a couple top-25 wins and, at least right now, looks like it will have a great chance to play in another CFP.

As for LSU? It's facing a game against Texas A&M this weekend that could already put its playoff hopes on the brink of implosion.

That wasn't the plan. And now you wonder if Kiffin didn't fully realize what he was leaving behind.

Kiffin, of course, knew Chambliss was very good. As has been well-chronicled, he believed that after Ole Miss was eliminated from the CFP, he'd make his pitch for Chambliss to transfer and get him a temporary restraining order through the court system for a fifth year of eligibility.

But if you unwind how it all went down last fall, those familiar with Kiffin's mentality will tell you he decided he couldn't take the Ole Miss program much further than he already had.

On Oct. 18, the 6-0 Rebels were leading 35-26 at Georgia starting the fourth quarter. They blew the lead, losing 43-35, and you can imagine this inner monologue where Kiffin is telling himself that as well as he'd done to push Ole Miss into the top 10, they were always going to come up just short against the blue bloods. To win it all, you had to be at one of the so-called helmet schools.

There was evidence of that same thinking in some of Kiffin's posts on X last fall about Indiana, where he took shots at their ranking and schedule and suggested they would not be favored over a bunch of SEC teams even though the Hoosiers absolutely would have been favored over nearly all of them.

It probably never occurred to him that Indiana could win a national title last year — or that Ole Miss might do it this year.

Regardless of what happened last Saturday in Mississippi, it's too early to say definitively that Kiffin made a mistake. The season is long, with unpredictable twists and turns ahead.

But if Kiffin had stayed at Ole Miss with the same cast of characters, the narrative right now would be that he's never had a better team or a better shot to win it all.

It's literally what he worked his entire career for. And now somebody else is going to lead that journey while he tries to hang on to playoff hopes against a schedule that includes Texas, Alabama and Tennessee.

We can all look back on what-ifs in how we handle our lives and careers. But Kiffin took the LSU job, just like the USC job, because he was more thrilled by the idea of the next thing than clear-eyed about the reality of the current thing.

Kiffin may not regret going to USC once upon a time. But if Ole Miss and Chambliss win the national title, it will be hard to deny that he made the wrong choice.

articles.title: Week 4 college football betting, odds: 3 early bets to make right now
articles.summary: Our college football handicapper gives three early Week 4 wagers he likes.
articles.body:
Three weeks into the season, recency bias is driving a lot of these early numbers. One loud Saturday changes how the public sees a team, and the opening lines follow. Arkansas is laying nearly a touchdown to an unbeaten Tulsa team, the total in Morgantown keeps climbing after West Virginia and Oklahoma State each beat a ranked opponent this month, and nobody wants anything to do with Colorado after a 34-point loss. These biases are where we find value headed into Week 4.

Here are three early Week 4 college football wagers I like right now:

Arkansas finally gets a break in the schedule. The Razorbacks just lost at No. 15 Utah by 33 and to No. 2 Georgia by 28, and now they get a Group of Five team at home. I understand why people see a get-right spot.

But have you looked at Tulsa? The Golden Hurricane are 3-0 for the first time since 2008, and their Week 1 win was 24-10 over an Oklahoma State team that beat No. 6 Oregon as a 23.5-point underdog a week later. Tre Lamb's defense has allowed 27 points in three games and forced six turnovers, and the offense is running for 220 yards a game behind Damari Alston and Trequan Jones. That travels.

Arkansas is the team I have questions about. The Hogs ran for 17 yards against Georgia and are averaging 75 yards per game on the ground. Ryan Silverfield is rotating KJ Jackson and AJ Hill at quarterback, and he told ESPN at halftime on Saturday that playing both was the plan all along. They've already turned it over five times, and a trip to Texas A&M is waiting next week.

We make this Arkansas by 4.4. A favorite that can't run the ball has to throw to cover, and that's a tough task against a defense that's living on takeaways. I'll take the points with the team that's playing better football right now.

Oklahoma State at West Virginia (-2.5, 59.5)

These are the two best stories in the Big 12.

Oklahoma State went 1-11 last year, then snapped a 21-game losing streak against FBS teams by beating No. 6 Oregon 39-31 and followed it up by putting 59 on Murray State. West Virginia just beat No. 25 Virginia 38-27 as a double-digit underdog, with Michael Hawkins Jr. accounting for all five touchdowns. Everybody saw those scores, so this total opened at 58.5 and has already been bet up to 59.5. But look at how West Virginia actually plays.

The Mountaineers are running it 54 times a game and throwing it 14 — and, no, that's not a typo. Against Virginia, Cam Cook carried 30 times, Hawkins carried 18 more, and Rich Rodriguez said afterward that the key was running it when everybody in the stadium knew it was coming. Every one of those handoffs keeps the clock moving and keeps Oklahoma State QB Drew Mestemaker on the sideline.

The defenses are better than people think, too. West Virginia held Virginia to seven points after halftime, Oklahoma State is allowing 267 yards a game and the Cowboys' only road trip so far produced 10 points at Tulsa. We make this 58.2, and I think Rodriguez is going to hand it off 50 times and dare everyone to change the channel.

Deion Sanders called last week's 41-7 loss at Northwestern a "flat-out butt kicking," and I won't waste time arguing with him. Colorado turned it over three times in the first half, it's averaging more than nine penalties a game, and this spread has gone from Baylor -6.5 to -10 since it opened. I don't want either side of that. I do like the total, though.

Baylor is running 84 plays a game and throwing for 306 yards, and the Bears scored 44 and 36 points, respectively, the last two weeks with a backup quarterback. DJ Lagway has been out with an ankle injury, and all Nate Bennett did against Louisiana Tech was go 21 of 24 for 253 yards and three touchdowns. Whichever one plays, the offense is fine.

Colorado's offense isn't as bad as seven points looks, either. Julian Lewis has 658 yards and six touchdowns, and the Buffaloes put 52 on Weber State two weeks ago. If this spread is anywhere close to right, Colorado is going to be throwing from behind for most of the afternoon, and Baylor's tempo means there will be plenty of possessions to do it with. We make this total 57.6. The last time these two played, in 2024, it took a Hail Mary and overtime to settle it at 38-31.

articles.title: Antiviolencia pide sanción de un año para los agresores del fan de la selección en Bilbao
articles.standfirst: Con motivo de la final del Mundial entre España-Argentina del pasado mes de julio
articles.summary: Con motivo de la final del Mundial entre España-Argentina del pasado mes de julio
articles.body: La Comisión Permanente de la Comisión Estatal contra la Violencia, el Racismo, la Xenofobia y la Intolerancia en el Deporte, reunida este martes en la sede del Consejo Superior de Deportes (CSD), ha acordado diversas propuestas de sanción. Entre ellas destaca la de 5.000 euros y prohibición de acceso a los recintos deportivos por un periodo de 12 meses a tres individuos que agredieron con violencia y sin mediar palabra a un aficionado que vestía una camiseta de la selección española cuando este se encontraba sentado en la plaza Emilio Campuzano de Bilbao a la espera del comienzo del encuentro España - Argentina de la final del Mundial de fútbol (19/07/2026). Igualmente hay propuestas de sanción de 10.000 euros y prohibición de acceso a los recintos deportivos por un periodo de 12 meses a dos aficionados radicales que increparon e intimidaron a un menor de edad por llevar una camiseta del Real Madrid. Cuando el menor se dirigía desde los vomitorios de la grada norte a su localidad en compañía de sus familiares, numerosos aficionados presentes en la grada secundaron la acción de los radicales, profiriendo insultos de índole racista y amenazas de muerte contra el menor con ocasión del encuentro Racing – Elche (28/08/2026). Propuestas de sanción de 5.000 euros y prohibición de acceso a los recintos deportivos por un periodo de 12 meses a seis aficionados visitantes que, una vez finalizado el partido y en las inmediaciones del estadio, agredieron e intimidaron a varios aficionados locales con ocasión del encuentro Almería - Castellón (09/06/2026). Propuestas de sanción de 5.000 euros y prohibición de acceso a los recintos deportivos por un periodo de 12 meses a cuatro individuos que participaron activamente en un enfrentamiento entre aficionados radicales de ideologías enfrentadas en la ciudad deportiva del Mallorca con ocasión del encuentro amistoso entre Mallorca y At. Baleares (15/08/2026). Propuestas de sanción de 5.000 euros y prohibición de acceso a los recintos deportivos por un periodo de 12 meses a dos individuos que participaron con violencia en un altercado con los vigilantes de seguridad tras negarse a ser cacheados en el acceso al estadio con ocasión del Celta - Osasuna (28/08/2026). articles.title: De Jong sigue los plazos marcados: se espera su vuelta tras el parón
articles.standfirst: Su evolución es correcta, pero los profesionales van con máxima cautela con el neerlandés
articles.summary: Su evolución es correcta, pero los profesionales van con máxima cautela con el neerlandés
articles.body: En la enfermería del Barcelona hay cuatro jugadores: De Jong, Roony, Joan García y Christensen. El centrocampista neerlandés es el que lleva más tiempo alejado de los terrenos de juego como consecuencia de una rotura en el ligamento interno de la rodilla. Pero su evolución sigue los prudentes plazos marcados, y la idea con la que trabaja el club es que se pueda sumar al equipo tras el parón. El centrocampista azulgrana se lesionó el pasado verano, durante el Mundial. Como él mismo explicó hace unas semanas. "Alguien cayó sobre mí en un entrenamiento. Me hice pruebas y salió que había un pequeño problema en la rodilla, y me dijeron que podía seguir jugando, que tendría algo de dolor, pero que podía continuar jugando. Me aseguraron que no podía ir a peor. Pero luego me hice otra prueba y mostró que la lesión era ahora más grave que cuando me hice la hice en Estados Unidos. Fue muy duro porque no me lo esperaba. Estoy muy jodido", comentó Frenkie de Jong. El internacional neerlandés, de 29 años, apostó por seguir un tratamiento conservador, a pesar de que en el Barcelona había voces que le recomendaban pasar por el quirófano. Pero De Jong optó por no hacerlo, y Flick y el Barça lo aceptaron y apoyaron. Su recuperación es lenta, pero, por el momento, su evolución se ajusta a los plazos marcados. La idea es que vaya incrementando estos días las cargas, como comenzar a tocar balón en algunas sesiones, para que tras el parón pueda sumarse al trabajo con el grupo. No tiene, no obstante, aún una fecha marcada para su regreso. En la entidad van con mucha cautela con la recuperación de De Jong. Pese a que sus sensaciones son positivas y se van cumpliendo los plazos, estos son bastantes prudentes por el miedo a un recaída o a dar un paso atrás... Su incorporación al grupo será, así mismo, muy progresiva. Lleva muchos meses sin ritmo de competición. Además, su encaje en el equipo será complicado a causa de la gran competencia. Uno de los capitanes culés rivaliza con Pedri, Rodri, Bernal, Gavi...

articles.title: Tebas responde al comunicado del Madrid que le señalaba: "Respeto a todos, subordinación a ninguno"
articles.standfirst: El presidente de LaLiga escribe una larga contestación al club presidido por Florentino Pérez
articles.summary: El presidente de LaLiga escribe una larga contestación al club presidido por Florentino Pérez
articles.body: Javier Tebas, presidente de LaLiga, ha respondido en redes sociales al durísimo comunicado del Real Madrid asegurando que no hace más que dañar la imagen de la propia Liga "con sus salidas de tono" y pidiendo, entre otras cosas, su recambio al frente del organismo. "Coincido plenamente en una frase: el presidente de LaLiga no es el dueño de la competición. El presidente del Real Madrid tampoco", arranca Tebas. "Representar a todos los clubes exige defender la igualdad y la equidad entre ellos. También cuando se sostiene que «LaLiga no vale nada» sin el Real Madrid o que los árbitros perjudican «al negocio que les da de comer». Sobre esas afirmaciones, que motivaron mi respuesta, su comunicado no dice una palabra", afirma sobre la nota del Madrid. "Ahora se escudan en que respondí a un periodista «independiente». Pero ni el relato es nuevo ni lo es la estrategia de desviar la atención de otros problemas. Llevan años haciéndolo desde Real Madrid TV y a través de sus portaCOCes, hablando y escribiendo de una Liga adulterada jornada tras jornada. No pretendan presentar como una opinión ajena el discurso que alimentan desde su propia televisión y desde las instancias del club", afirma sobre los famosos videos de Real Madrid TV. "Reclaman que contribuya a generar confianza en la imparcialidad de la competición. Precisamente por eso rechazo el relato de que los árbitros están dirigidos contra el Real Madrid. Criticar una decisión arbitral es legítimo. Convertir cada perjuicio en prueba de una persecución es otra cosa. ¿Eso genera confianza o daña la imagen del fútbol español?", afirma Tebas sobre la acusación blanca de no generar confianza en las instituciones que deben garantizar la imparcialidad de la competición. "Confunden neutralidad con independencia. Si por neutralidad entienden no tomar partido ante nada, ni siquiera entre lo que está bien y lo que está mal, están pidiendo que renuncie a mi responsabilidad. La independencia exige decidir con criterio propio, sin presiones ni subordinaciones, aplicando las mismas reglas a todos y defendiendo el interés común. Eso implica tomar decisiones y posicionarse, aunque al Real Madrid no le guste". "Defender los intereses de un club no significa asumir su discurso. Y representar a todos tampoco significa obedecer al más poderoso. Hay que defender los intereses de la competición, de LaLiga. Ni soy el dueño de LaLiga ni voy a gestionarla como si perteneciera a un solo club. Respeto a todos. Subordinación a ninguno".

articles.title: El United no desiste con JJ Gabriel... pero ya busca sustituto
articles.standfirst: El club inglés se interesa por Mezian Mesloub y Gabriel Rajkovic
articles.summary: El club inglés se interesa por Mezian Mesloub y Gabriel Rajkovic
articles.body: El club inglés está haciendo todo lo posible para que JJ Gabriel recule y decida quedarse en Mánchester. El futbolista no tiene un contrato profesional, al ser menor de 16 años, y todo apunta a que dejará el club, por lo que ya se han puesto manos a la obra. La entidad que entrena Michael Carrick ha puesto el ojo en dos futuras promesas: Mezian Mesloub y Gabriel Rajkovic. El primero sorprendió al mundo entero hace unas pocas semanas en la Champions League. El futbolistas del Lens de 16 años de edad entró frente al Slavia de Praga y con una asistencia, ayudó a la remontada de su equipo. Pero lo que sorprendió del portugués fue su gran parecido al estilo de juego de Lamine Yamal. Según Teamtalk, el Manchester United está haciendo un trabajo exhaustivo para incorporar la perla a su cantera, al igual que Arsenal y Chelsea. Sin embargo, algunos competidores llevan ventajas. Los equipos de la Premier tienen prohibido fichar a jugadores europeos menores de 18 años que no sean de federaciones de Reino Unido salvo excepciones. El PSG y el Mónaco son otros de los equipos que quiere hacerse con Mesloub, y estar ya disputando la Ligue 1, puede suponer una ventaja para hacerse con sus servicios. En el punto de mira también está Gabriel Rajkovic, futbolista de 15 años del Valerenga. Según The Sun, el Manchester United envió un ojeador para verle, al igual que el FC Barcelona. Al igual que JJ Gabriel, Rajkovic es un jugador con buena técnica con ambos pies, aunque este ocupa la posición de extremo. Ya ha jugado 14 partidos en la máxima competición noruega, en los que ha podido marcar dos tantos. Nacido y representante de la selección de Noruega, también puede llegar ajuar con Serbia, Bélica y Marruecos. Según fuentes del país nórdico, el traspaso podría cerrarse en 16 millones de euros. Rajkovic ya habría rechazado varias ofertas de grandes clubes importantes y no tendría prisas en abandonar su país, teniendo contrato con el Valerenga hasta 2028. Dos futbolistas por los que deberán esperar y pelearse con otros grandes clubes para incorporar a sus filas ante la salida de JJ Gabriel.

articles.title: Colorado's Ben Finneseth Apologizes for Ripping Northwestern's Stadium in Viral Video
articles.summary: Colorado senior defensive back Ben Finneseth is walking back his comments from a viral video criticizing Northwestern's temporary stadium.
articles.body:
Colorado senior defensive back Ben Finneseth is walking back his comments from a viral video criticizing Northwestern's temporary stadium.

Buffaloes head coach Deion Sanders called Finnseth up to apologize during a Tuesday press conference.

"It was childish. It was a stupid thing that I said. It won't happen again... It will be much more mature moving forward," Finnseth said.

The video initially shared by Kamran Nia appeared to show Colorado players comparing the atmosphere of the 12,000-person stadium to a library ahead of last Saturday's game against the Wildcats.

Northwestern, which is playing at a temporary location during ongoing renovations of Ryan Field, went on to claim a 41-7 win over the Buffaloes.

Colorado's offense turned over the ball four times, including on the first two interception of quarterback Julian Lewis' career, while the defense allowed Northwestern to rack up 423 total yards.

The win marked Northwestern's largest margin of victory against a power conference opponent since 2020, per ESPN's Pete Thamel .

Sanders said after Saturday's loss he "got on" some of his players for laughing after the loss.

When asked Tuesday about his players' reaction to the loss, Sanders said there were "a few guys not on the team anymore."

Saturday's win marked the end of Northwestern football's tenure at Martin Stadium, which welcomed the team for five games in the 2025 season and hosted non-conference matchups this fall against South Dakota State and Colorado.

The renovation project at Ryan Field, which has a budget of $870 million, features a capacity of 35,000 seats and a 520,000 square-foot increase over the old stadium.

Northwestern will now hit the road for a game against No. 5 Indiana this Friday before turning home for the team's debut at the new Ryan Field Oct. 2 against No. 13 Penn State.

Colorado is also scheduled for a road game this week at Baylor before returning to Folsom Field, which has a capacity of around 53,000, to play its highest-ranked opponent of the season so far in No. 11 Texas Tech.

articles.title: Pellegrini y su cuerpo técnico recorren el Camino de Santiago tras llevar al Betis a la Champions
articles.standfirst: El Ingeniero y sus colaboradores completan 40 kilómetros cumpliendo una promesa
articles.summary: El Ingeniero y sus colaboradores completan 40 kilómetros cumpliendo una promesa
articles.body: Manuel Pellegrini y su cuerpo técnico ya han cumplido la promesa que se hicieron la pasada temporada: completar parte del Camino de Santiago si conseguían clasificar al Betis para la Champions League. El regreso del conjunto verdiblanco a la máxima competición continental más de dos décadas después tuvo premio deportivo y también una particular celebración que el técnico chileno y sus colaboradores tenían pendiente. La oportunidad perfecta llegó este fin de semana. El Betis visitó el domingo al Deportivo de la Coruña en la séptima jornada de Liga y, una vez terminado el encuentro, el calendario ofrecía unas condiciones inmejorables para saldar aquella deuda. Los verdiblancos afrontan ahora un paréntesis de casi tres semanas sin competición liguera por la fecha FIFA de selecciones, por lo que Pellegrini y varios miembros de su cuerpo técnico decidieron prolongar su estancia en Galicia y ponerse en marcha hacia Santiago. En total, el grupo ha permanecido un par de días recorriendo alrededor de 40 kilómetros a pie en las etapas finales del Camino, con la plaza del Obradoiro como destino. Allí, frente a la Catedral de Santiago de Compostela, inmortalizaron el momento con una fotografía compartida en Instagram por Toni Doblas, entrenador de porteros, después de completar el recorrido y cumplir así la promesa que se habían marcado meses atrás si conseguían el gran reto deportivo del pasado curso. Una experiencia muy diferente a las habituales jornadas de entrenamiento, análisis de rivales y partidos que forman parte del día a día del cuerpo técnico verdiblanco. El Camino, además de su origen religioso, se ha convertido con el paso de los siglos en una ruta recorrida por peregrinos de todo el mundo por motivos espirituales, personales o deportivos, y su llegada a la plaza del Obradoiro constituye el final simbólico para quienes tienen Santiago como destino. En el caso de Pellegrini y sus colaboradores, el recorrido tenía un significado muy concreto. Era la manera elegida para celebrar un objetivo especialmente importante: devolver al Betis a la Champions. El técnico chileno ha aprovechado así de una manera muy particular este primer tramo del parón. Después de completar el Camino y cumplir la promesa, Pellegrini y su equipo de trabajo podrán disfrutar de unos días antes de comenzar a preparar el regreso a la competición, con un calendario nuevamente exigente y el Betis inmerso esta temporada en el desafío de competir entre los mejores clubes de Europa.

articles.title: Deion Sanders Says 'A Few Guys' Were Dismissed from Colorado Roster After Northwestern Blowout Loss
articles.summary: Colorado coach Deion Sanders didn't take the team's 41-7 loss to Northwestern lightly.
articles.body:
Colorado coach Deion Sanders didn't take the team's 41-7 loss to Northwestern lightly.

Sanders told reporters Tuesday that "a few guys" have been dismissed from the team. He elaborated slightly and said they were removed for conduct detrimental to the team:

Linebacker Tyler Martinez and defensive back Randon Fontenette offered their thoughts on the situation:

Sanders famously set the tone for his tenure during his first team meeting after getting hired in December 2022. He told the assembled group of players that "I'm bringing my luggage with me and it's Louis (Vuitton)."

Coach Prime made it clear he expected a certain set of standards, and anybody who didn't meet them would be surplus to requirements.

Dismissing players after the season kicked off will always raise some questions, though. This may reflect the increased pressure Sanders is feeling after a 3-9 finish in 2025.

The Buffaloes are still generating some excitement around Boulder, but the buzz isn't anywhere close to what it was when Coach Prime arrived. The results have to follow at some point. Heading into Year 4 of the Sanders era, Colorado is 18-22 with him at the helm.

Beating Georgia Tech 14-13 in the opener was encouraging, but getting hammered by Northwestern will have some fans wondering whether they're in for more of the same. The Buffs committed four turnovers and gave up 423 yards.

Sanders didn't disclose who got the boot. Their identities may be clear when Colorado walks onto the field Saturday to play Baylor.

articles.title: Iker Bravo: "Me han caído más h*** de las que merezco, ahora con 21 años quiero ser el mejor padre del mundo"
articles.standfirst: El futbolista del Watford se sincera en el programa 'Otra Ronda' de Radio MARCA
articles.summary: El futbolista del Watford se sincera en el programa 'Otra Ronda' de Radio MARCA
articles.body: Iker Bravo vuelve a sonreír. Inglaterra y la paternidad le están sentando bien. A sus 21 años, el delantero ha encontrado en Inglaterra el escenario que necesitaba para recuperar su mejor versión después de unos últimos años marcados por los cambios de equipo y la falta de continuidad. Tras sus etapas en Udinese y Las Palmas, el futbolista ha aterrizado en el Watford, donde está teniendo protagonismo y ha encontrado una nueva posición como mediapunta. Desde la concentración de la Selección española Sub-21, donde ha regresado tras su buen inicio de temporada, atendió a Carlos Vicente 'Chitu' y Marcos Bernat en 'Otra Ronda' de Radio MARCA. “Ha sido todo increíble porque he sido padre, ha sido lo mejor que me ha podido pasar en la vida”, explicó Bravo al recordar sus últimos meses. El futbolista se convirtió en padre a los 21 años y reconoce que la llegada de su hijo Enzo ha cambiado sus prioridades. “Desde que soy padre, si te soy sincero, prefiero ser el mejor padre del mundo para mis hijos. Que nunca les falte nada, que siempre tengan salud y que sean los más felices. Y si ya soy el mejor jugador del mundo, de p*** madre”, aseguró. En lo deportivo, el cambio de aires también le ha permitido recuperar sensaciones. Bravo reconoce que está “volviendo a disfrutar jugando a fútbol”, algo que buscaba después de una etapa complicada. En Watford ha encontrado la confianza de su entrenador y una posición en la mediapunta en la que se siente especialmente cómodo. “Creo que mi posición en el fútbol actual y todo como está es media punta”, explicó. El propio jugador relaciona directamente esa confianza con su rendimiento: “Cuando juego y estoy feliz, juego bien”. Bravo también explicó qué ha encontrado en el fútbol inglés que le está permitiendo explotar sus cualidades. “Pasado el minuto 60 es todo transición. Para arriba, para abajo, para arriba, para abajo”, señaló. Un escenario que, según el delantero, le permite tener más espacios para crear, atacar y ser protagonista. Después de haber pasado por Alemania, España e Italia, el jugador no oculta su satisfacción con su nueva aventura. “Inglaterra me encanta”, reconoció. De hecho, cuando le preguntaron si le gustaría regresar a España, su respuesta fue clara: “Sinceramente, no. Ahora mismo no, pero en un futuro, obviamente”. Su objetivo pasa por seguir disfrutando de su presente en Watford y aprovechar la oportunidad con la Sub-21. Bravo también habló de una etapa en la que reconoce haber sufrido. “Estos últimos dos añitos, año y medio, han sido muy duros para mí. Ha sido mucho cambio, mucho ‘te quiero, no te quiero’, ahora por ahí, ahora por allá”, explicó. Ahora, su intención es dejar atrás todo aquello y centrarse en disfrutar. El futbolista también recordó el papel que tuvo Álvaro Arbeloa durante su formación en el Real Madrid. “Arbeloa me habló como si fuera mi padre. Y eso fue lo que a mí me hizo reflexionar”, contó. De aquel periodo se quedó con una enseñanza que considera fundamental para su carrera: los buenos hábitos. “Para tener una carrera exitosa de unos 15 años, tienes que tener unos buenos hábitos sobre todo”, afirmó. Su buen momento en Inglaterra le ha abierto de nuevo las puertas de la Selección española Sub-21. Bravo se mostró orgulloso de formar parte de una generación a la que ve con muchísimo potencial. “Es un equipazo y además de ser un equipazo dentro del campo es un equipazo afuera”, aseguró. El delantero afronta ahora la concentración con la intención de disfrutar del momento y centrarse en el día a día. “Ahora estoy aquí con la Sub-21 a disfrutar la Sub-21. Después volveré a Watford a disfrutar Watford partido a partido”, explicó. A la hora de hablar de su techo, Bravo no se pone límites, aunque es consciente de que todavía tiene mucho camino por recorrer. “Yo confío muchísimo en mí y sé que tengo el talento para hacer una carrera muy bonita. Pero lo tengo que demostrar. Aún no he demostrado nada”, reconoció. Y si hay algo que resume su actual momento vital es el mensaje que quiso dejarle a su hijo Enzo para el futuro: “Me ha dado muchas fuerzas en mi vida en un momento donde no encontraba sentido a lo que estaba haciendo”. Su deseo para él es sencillo: “Quiero que sea la persona más feliz del mundo y que siempre, siempre, siempre todo lo que haga, lo haga para ser feliz y que sea buena persona con buenos valores”.

articles.title: Ville Koski se consolida como hombre fuerte de Quique
articles.standfirst: El finlandés ha formado de inicio en todos los partidos de Liga. Desde su desembarco en el fútbol español, el Alavés ha dejado la puerta a cero en el 50% de sus encuentros como titular.
articles.summary: El finlandés ha formado de inicio en todos los partidos de Liga. Desde su desembarco en el fútbol español, el Alavés ha dejado la puerta a cero en el 50% de sus encuentros como titular.
articles.body: Ville Koski se ha ganado por méritos propios ser una pieza imprescindible para Quique Sánchez Flores en el eje de la zaga. El central finlandés ha pasado de ser la última opción en la defensa a convertirse en uno de los tres jugadores de campo que ha sido titular en todos los partidos esta temporada junto a Tenaglia y Rebbach. Su rendimiento, explica entre otras cosas, el salto cualitativo que ha experimentado el Alavés en el aspecto defensivo. El ex del Istra 1961 aterrizó en el último mercado invernal para reforzar una defensa mermada por la falta de efectivos. Llegó lesionado y su primera titularidad no tuvo lugar hasta la antepenúltima jornada ante el Barcelona. Lejos de acusar la falta de minutos, Koski firmó una gran actuación ante el campeón de Liga y desde entonces nadie le ha bajado del once inicial. Fue clave en los dos triunfos que certificaron la permanencia en la recta final del pasado curso y también lo está siendo en el arranque de esta temporada. La presencia del finlandés dota de mayor consistencia al Alavés. Su fortaleza en los duelos aéreos le convierten en una pieza muy valorada por Quique en una defensa que no está sobrada de centímetros. Además, Koski no está desentonando cuando el técnico adelanta la línea defensiva, pese a que no es un defensa veloz y puede sufrir cuando el rival le coge la espalda. Lo suple con agresividad y tratando de incomodar a su marca en el cuerpo a cuerpo para que no pueda girar. Koski se encuentra más cómodo en ese 5-3-2 que ha planteado en la mayoría de partidos el preparador babazorro, escoltado por otros dos jugadores en el centro de la defensa. Con el futbolista finlandés en el once titular, el Alavés ha dejado el 50% de las veces su portería a cero. En cinco de los diez encuentros de inicio de Koski, los de Quique no han encajado goles. Sus inicios no fueron sencillos, pero la adaptación al fútbol español es toda una realidad y su rendimiento cada vez está más consolidado.

articles.title: La impresora
articles.standfirst: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.summary: Sobran los motivos, por Alberto R. Barbero
articles.body: Tiene cierta lógica que, por lo que pueda pasar, circule por el mundo con impresora un Real Madrid al que patrocina HP, véanse por ejemplo las mangas de sus futbolistas. No tiene tanta, visto lo visto, que el acuerdo entre el club y la multinacional citara en su momento una voluntad de "mejorar la sociedad y promover la dignidad". No parece al menos que fuera ésa la intención de José Mourinho cuando tiró de la tecnología que ofrece Hewlett-Packard, apellidos a los que corresponden las siglas en cuestión, para presentarse en el auditorio del Metropolitano con lo que él consideraba pruebas irrefutables del atropello, impresas sobre la hoja de alineaciones que intercambian los delegados antes de que la pelota eche a rodar. Y con el papel hizo un papelón. Primero porque a buenas horas aparecía con imágenes fijas para lo que el personal había contemplado ya en movimiento. Segundo porque, por mucho que acumule antecedentes desde su primera etapa, la 'performance' recordaba demasiado a los lamentables y habituales teatrillos con que tienen a mal obsequiarnos los políticos de turno. Y tercero porque el batiburrillo (interesado desde el momento en que olvidaba tantas acciones o partidos como los que recordaba) apenas conseguía disfrazar el empeño de que se hablara de cualquier persona o cosa menos de él. Lo mismo que Mou utilizó su alocución para juzgar el desempeño de Ortiz Arias, y prácticamente nada más que eso, el del silbato podría haber comparecido para valorar la escasa aportación del inquilino del banquillo visitante al que se suponía principal objetivo de su equipo: ganar el partido. Simeone pudo equivocarse (o no) en alineación y gestión de los últimos minutos, pero entre una y otra dejó un plan para "llevar el partido donde podamos hacer daño" y un cambio, el de Koke por Pubill, que sirvió a su vez para cambiarlo casi todo. ¿Qué dejó Mourinho? Una impresora. Ciertamente impresionante. PD: ¿Qué habrá sido del sindicato arbitral que tan valiente se mostró con Pepe Bordalás?

articles.title: Cardiovanguardia 2026 convierte Valencia en el epicentro de la cardiología y la medicina
articles.standfirst: Se trata de la cita científica de cardiología y medicina del deporte más importante de España
articles.summary: Se trata de la cita científica de cardiología y medicina del deporte más importante de España
articles.body: EEl Ilustre Colegio Oficial de Médicos de Valencia (ICOMV) albergará en la Sala Chulia Campos este viernes, 25 de septiembre de 2026, a partir de las 11 horas, la cita científica de cardiología y medicina del deporte más importante de España este año: el curso Cardiovanguardia Valencia 2026. El evento, avalado por la Sociedad Valenciana de Cardiología, reunirá a una selección élite de profesionales nacionales e internacionales para debatir de forma integral los últimos avances en la salud cardiovascular aplicados al deporte, y está organizado por los Dres. De la Guía y Diaz, actuales coordinadores del grupo de trabajo de cardiología del deporte de la Sociedad Española de Cardiología El congreso abarca diferentes mesas y una conferencia magistral, donde se debatirán temas relacionados con el cuidado del deportista —desde el atleta recreacional hasta la alta competición—, hasta pacientes con problemas de corazón. La reunión destaca por un cartel de ponentes que incluye a figuras de la élite mundial. Entre ellos se encuentran el Dr. Iñigo San Millán (director de rendimiento del Athletic Club de Bilbao), el Dr. Didac Navarro, profesional del equipo ciclista UAE Team Emirates XRG, entre otros, quienes compartirán su experiencia en la monitorización y optimización del rendimiento en deportistas de la talla mundial. Así mismo, se abordarán temáticas de gran impacto transversal, como la salud cardiovascular y los mitos en la mujer deportista (presentación del documento de Consenso sobre ejercicio y salud cardiovascular en la mujer), el uso de la inteligencia artificial aplicada al deporte y los criterios de aptitud en profesiones de riesgo como son los militares; habrá espacio para analizar la nutrición, los límites de la suplementación y los riesgos cardiacos en el culturismo, contando con una conferencia magistral del prestigioso catedrático Dr. José Ramón González Juanatey, candidato oficial a la presidencia de la Federación Mundial del Corazón para las elecciones de este otoño de 2026. La asistencia al evento es totalmente gratuita, con inscripción al correo electrónico secretaria.tecnica@svcardio.org.

articles.title: Schröder no es suficiente ante el PSG
articles.standfirst: El Real Madrid empató en casa ante el conjunto galo en un partido en el que pudo hacer más
articles.summary: El Real Madrid empató en casa ante el conjunto galo en un partido en el que pudo hacer más
articles.body: El Real Madrid arrancó la fase Liga de la Women’s Champions League con un empate (1-1) ante el PSG en el Di Stéfano que sabe a poco. El tanto inicial de Schröder fue contestado por otro de Karchaoui desde los once metros y el duelo repartió un punto para cada equipo. No pudo empezar mejor la cosa para las locales. Apenas habían transcurrido 98 segundos desde el pitido inicial cuando Schröder, a pase de Caruso, estrenaba el marcador. El PSG intentó reaccionar de la mano -pies en este caso- de Karchaoui, capitana y alma del conjunto galo, que penalizó una pérdida en la medular con un pase entre líneas que no supo aprovechar Feller; y una falta botada desde la frontal mal rematada por Isabela. El partido se ensució tanto en el campo como en la grada, donde los hinchas del PSG -ubicados a escasos metros de la Grada de Animación del Real Madrid- tuvieron que ser reubicados por seguridad tras gestos poco deportivos entre ambas aficiones. Hubo que esperar a la media hora de acción para advertir un nuevo intento de remate, otra vez con la firma de Felicia, que esta vez se fue excesivamente desviado. El paso por vestuarios no cambió el sino del encuentro. El PSG fue dueño del balón y el Real Madrid, en bloque bajo en su propio campo, se limitaba a sorprender a la contra con la velocidad de Eva Navarro, la magia de Caicedo o la determinación de Schröder, que tuvo el segundo nuevamente en sus botas. La sueca falló un mano a mano con Kiedrzynek, estrelló un balón en el poste en una contra lanzada por Linda y falló en el remate asistida otra vez por la colombiana. A falta de 20 minutos para el final, la árbitra señaló penalti a favor de las visitantes por una falta de Lakrar sobre Morissaint. El lanzamiento lo ejecutó Karchaoui, que no falló a su cita con el gol. El Real Madrid apretó los dientes y pisó el acelerador. Quesada, que había apostado por Athenea, dio entrada a Beerensteyn. Esta vez no se alinearon los astros y el conjunto blanco se fue con un punto que sabe a poco.

articles.title: Man City hold Bayern to start Women's Champions League, Arsenal win late
articles.summary: Manchester City fought from two goals down to grab a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich on Tuesday to start their Women's Champions League season, while Mariona Calde...
articles.body:
Manchester City fought from two goals down to grab a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich on Tuesday to start their Women's Champions League season, while Mariona Caldentey was the hero as Arsenal left it late in their opener.

Bayern raced into a 2-0 lead thanks to Giulia Gwinn 's early strike and a Kerstin Casparij own goal inside the first 30 minutes.

Beth Mead halved the deficit for the Women's Super League champions on the stroke of half-time.

City looked set to begin the league phase with a loss, as Khadija Shaw was denied from the spot by Bayern goalkeeper Ena Mahmutovic in the second period.

But German forward Carlotta Wamser popped up with four minutes remaining to ensure the spoils were shared in Bavaria.

"It was a game of two halves, I think. (The first half) was probably not good enough for our standards," Mead told UEFA.

"But again we showed what the team is about, showed our character."

Arsenal, the 2025 Champions League winners, made a faltering start to their bid to recover the continent's premier club title.

Renee Slegers's side needed an injury-time penalty from Spain international Caldentey to nab a 1-0 win at home to Danes HB Koge.

The Gunners looked certain to be heading for a goalless stalemate until new signing Selina Cerci went down in the box under Yukina Sakabe's 92nd-minute challenge.

A Sakina Karchaoui penalty inside the final 20 minutes ensured Paris Saint-Germain left the Estadio Alfredo Di Stefano with a 1-1 draw after Felicia Schroeder's second-minute opener for Real Madrid .

Inter Milan got the better of Swedish side Hacken 1-0 -- Haley Bugeja's fifth-minute goal was enough to give the home side three points.

A brace either side of half-time by Marit Bratberg Lund gave Benfica a 2-1 win at Juventus , despite the hosts scoring late through Alba Redondo .

Defending champions Barcelona begin Champions League life in the post-Alexia Putellas era on Wednesday when they host Paris FC.

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith Once Again Set for Multiple MNF ‘Countdown’ Appearances
articles.summary: Smith made his 2026 debut ahead of Rams-Giants on Monday.
articles.body:
Stephen A. Smith is returning to ESPN's Monday Night Countdown .

Smith is expected to appear on three or four episodes of the pregame show this season, an ESPN spokesman confirmed to Front Office Sports .

On Monday night, Smith made his first appearance of the season with host Scott Van Pelt and castmates Pat McAfee, Marcus Spears, Jason Kelce , and Jason McCourty from Los Angeles before the network's telecast of Giants-Rams. As a special guest, Smith popped up on the Monday Night Countdown desk about 20 minutes into the show, where he dapped up Van Pelt, McAfee, and Spears.

After the Rams' 28–6 victory, the featured commentator and executive producer of First Take immediately flew back to New York to host his popular weekday morning show.

Smith debuted on Monday Night Countdown last season, appearing three times with Van Pelt & Co. He was absent, however, from the Countdown desk ahead of ESPN's Week 1 telecast of the Chiefs' victory over the Broncos , raising some questions as to whether his role on the program was one season and done. Monday also marked Smith's first Countdown appearance alongside McAfee, who is new to the pregame show this season , uniting arguably ESPN's two biggest stars.

Growing up in Hollis, Queens, the native New Yorker dreamed of following in the footsteps of his idol Howard Cosell by covering the NFL.

When Smith negotiated his monster five-year, $100 million -plus contract extension in 2025, he specifically asked for and got the chance to work on ESPN's Monday Night Football coverage. Smith previously explained his idea to FOS during ESPN's Media Day in 2024.

"I don't want to insult the legacy of the great Howard Cosell, who's somebody that I idolized. But that's what I want to do," Smith told me . "When I think about the NFL, I'm not talking about being in the booth with Troy Aikman and Joe Buck. You don't mess with that chemistry; you leave that alone. But I'm unapologetic about what I want. I would love to be a part of Monday Night Football ."

Conversely, Smith dropped off Malika Andrews's NBA Countdown pregame show last season once TNT Sports licensed Charles Barkley's Inside the NBA to serve as ABC/ESPN's premier pregame hoops show.

The big question now around Monday Night Football is what happens with Troy Aikman ? While Joe Buck has signed a six-year contract extension worth $108 million, there's been little to no progress on a new deal for the ex-Cowboys QB, who's now in the last season of his original five-year, $90 million deal.

It's a tricky, delicate situation given that Aikman and Buck are poised to call ESPN's historic first Super Bowl at SoFi Stadium on Feb. 14, 2027. Monday Night Football , the granddaddy of all primetime sports programming, celebrated its 56th anniversary on Monday night.

"But it shows that Carlotta is in the penalty box as a left-back pretty often in the games and how she is playing.

"Beth Mead is involved in a lot of things and she is learning a little bit of a new role."

articles.title: How Texas Tech football first-time starters handled the spotlight
articles.summary: Texas Tech football had some starting lineup changes last week. Here's how Trey White, Davin Martin, BJ Jordan handled their first starts this year.
articles.body:
Texas Tech football watchers waited eight months to see what Trey White would bring to the Red Raiders' pass rush . Then they waited two weeks more after the transfer from San Diego State hurt late in fall camp.

White made his Tech debut on Friday, Sept. 18, getting credit for two tackles and a sack in the Red Raiders' 28-26 victory against Houston at Galaxy Stadium . White, a 6-foot-2, 255-pound edge defender has been dealing with a knee injury and revealed Tuesday, Sept. 22, that he actually had surgery three weeks ago.

"I feel great," he said, "good enough to be back on the field playing again, feeling pretty much like myself. And then once I'm able to get this brace off my leg, I'm good."

Photos of Texas Tech football hosting Houston in Big 12 play

No. 10 Tech (3-0) hosts Sam Houston State (1-2) at 11 a.m. Saturday, Sept. 26.

White, a fifth-year senior, had a combined 19 1/2 sacks the past two years for San Diego State, earning first-team all-Mountain West Conference recognition both seasons. So the Red Raiders were eager to see him as much as he was he was eager to see his new environment.

"Mike [Ramirez} and the training staff did a great job in preparing me," White said, "and getting me used to being back out there on the field before I suited up, making sure I was comfortable out there. Just being in that stadium with all the fans and my parents' first time seeing me play ever at the Galaxy Stadium, it was insane for them."

White's Tech debut was one of a few firsts in the Tech-Houston game. Safety Brenden Jordan made his season debut after missing the first two games for a team rules violation. Also, edge defender Jamond Mathis and cornerback Davin Martin made their first starts for Tech after transferring from Kent State and UT-San Antonio, respectively.

Martin's a 6-2, 185-pound senior from Klein Cain, and his first extended action happened to come against his hometown team.

"It was fun, especially when I got the start," he said. "On that team, I know a lot of those guys and those coaches, so it was fun. It was a physical game. I looked forward to it, and I'm glad we won."

Martin was in on four tackles and broke up two passes. He was among the 21 newcomers who joined the Red Raiders in January from the NCAA transfer portal.

"A lot, man," Martin said, "with my strength and my conditioning and my weight gain, just to how I play. I'm more physical now. Formation recognition, I can recognize formations and get one small, minor detail and I'll be able to play a little faster. Playing around other great players as well, it makes my job easier and it's more fun."

Jordan's one of the seasoned veterans on the Tech defense. The senior from Mansfield's streak of 15 consecutive starts ended with his having to sit the first two games. He picked up where he left off. Jordan and linebacker Ben Roberts were credited with a team-high 10 tackles apiece against Houston, Jordan's total including a team-high 8 solos.

"I think I did well," Jordan said. "I played hard. One of my main goals was just to go out there and play fast, play hard. So I think I did pretty good."

All off-season, Tech expected Jordan to anchor the secondary, starting at safety alongside juniors Peyton Morgan, Malik Esquerra or Oliver Miles III, all first-time starting candidates. Esquerra's started all three games at boundary safety, taking over the spot Cole Wisniewski manned last year. Jordan opened last week at field safety, where he played last season and where Morgan started the first two games.

While sitting those first two weeks, Jordan said he made the best of the situation.

"I was excited to watch them, honestly, seeing my team play," Jordan said. "It was frustrating a little bit, actually, but it wasn't bad at all. Seeing my guys play, supporting them all I could do and just helping the young guys to get better."

articles.summary: Largo vídeo de 4 minutos recordando "la liga peligrosamente preparada" y otras quejas colchoneras
articles.body: en una tarde de mucho movimiento en la sala de máquinas de Concha Espina, el Real Madrid también ha tenido tiempo de responder irónicamente al Atleti y su campaña en redes de 'Stop acoso arbitral' o el de "tres semanas ahora con la maquinaria a tope" con la imagen de José Mourinho y sus quejas tras el derbi. En un largo vídeo, emitido por Real Madrid TV, se recuperan momentos de los últimos años en los que "si les perjudican, ya no respetan tanto”, asegura la voz en off. “La memoria es corta; piden respeto para los árbitros, pero sólo a veces. Ahora exigen respeto, pero si no les gusta lo que ven, comunicado al canto”. Entre la colección de imágenes, Diego Simeone es el principal protagonista, sobre todo cuando calificó la Liga de “peligrosamente preparada para el Madrid” o su rueda de prensa tras la eliminatoria de Champions pidiendo a ver "que levante la mano quien haya visto un doble toque de Julián". El técnico también sale en otro momento caliente de un partido con frases o gestos gruesos hacia los árbitros. "Aquí respeto no hay mucho, más bien insultos a los árbitros" se oye también recordando un comunicado del equipo del Metropolitano tras otro derbi reciente con la frase “cualquiera que lo observe desde fuera, puede ver que desde hace década sucede lo mismo; el sistema es así, nos hemos acostumbrado”. O con aquel famoso tuit colchonero pidiendo "retuitea si quieres que se aplique el reglamento para todos", desde la cuenta oficial del Atleti. “Pides respeto, pero pones tuits cuando lo que sucede no es de tu agrado. El respeto desaparece cuando vienen mal dadas. Si te benefician respetas, si te perjudicas, ya no tanto”, se oye sobre imágenes de Arda Turan tirándole una bota a un linier. Por último recuerdan a Gregorio Manzano, ex entrenador del Atleti y ahora "designa a los árbitros".

articles.summary: League One and Two clubs thrash Premier League under-21 sides in the EFL Trophy group phase.
articles.body:
League One and League Two sides rained in goals against Premier League under-21 opposition in the EFL Trophy on Tuesday.

The competition, which is being sponsored for the next five seasons by US sandwich chain Jersey Mike's, saw 93 goals scored across 23 ties.

Newly promoted League Two side Rochdale's tie against Liverpool Under-21s in Northern Group H was briefly halted after 69 minutes due to fireworks being aimed into the ground from outside.

Will Wright, the 18-year-old former Salford striker, had earlier cancelled out Devante Rodney 's opener for the hosts with a stunning solo goal but 41-year-old Ian Henderson put Dale back ahead after the brief delay with the first goal of his 24th professional season and dinked a third moments later.

However, the Reds youngsters, who played with 10-men from the 21st minute after a red card for Senegalese defender Mor Talla Ndiaye, dug deep to score four and six minutes into stoppage time to snatch a draw and added insult to injury by nicking the penalty shootout 7-6 in sudden death to secure a bonus point.

Russell Martin fielded a strong Leicester side who raced into a 5-0 lead before half-time against Fulham Under-21s, with Bosnian striker Admir Bristric scoring a hat-trick inside 34 minutes and Tommy Watson adding two more.

The Cottagers pulled one back before Bobby De Cordova-Reid netted against his former club to add to his three first-half assists, while Watson came within inches of a claim to the match ball as he hit the post in the dying moments.

The other game in Southern Group B also finished 6-1, with Michael Mellon scoring a hat-trick in Stevenage's big win at Walsall .

Accrington came from 2-0 down against Sunderland Under-21s to snatch a last-gasp equaliser in a 3-3 draw through Stefan Mols and then secured a bonus point in Northern Group A with a 3-1 win on spot-kicks.

Luton midfielder Jordan Clark scored a hat-trick on his 33rd birthday as the Hatters thrashed Ipswich Town Under-21s 6-0 in Southern Group D while Caleb Watts scored twice as Plymouth ran out 5-1 winners against Crystal Palace in Southern Group E.

Jack Lankester netted two as Crewe Alexandra thumped Aston Villa 's under-21s 4-1 in Northern Group B, while Nick Powell bagged both as Bradford came from behind to beat Newcastle's youngsters 2-1 and join them at the top of Group C.

Emeka Adiele's first goal for Burton put them ahead against Nottingham Forest Under-21s but the visitors came back to level and then pinched the bonus point on penalties, though they stay behind Northern Group F leaders Notts County, who beat Grimsby 2-1.

Barnsley were 4-0 down with 10 minutes to go at home to Leeds in Group G but rallied to score three times in seven minutes, though they could not find an equaliser.

articles.title: Wasteful Arsenal need late penalty to beat Koge
articles.summary: Mariona Caldentey scores from the spot in stoppage time to snatch victory for Arsenal against HB Koge in the Women's Champions League.
articles.body:
Mariona Caldentey scored a stoppage-time penalty to secure victory for a wasteful Arsenal at home to Danish side HB Koge in the first game of their Women's Champions League campaign.

Arsenal, who had struggled in front of goal against a side made up of several part-time players, were heading towards a disappointing draw when Caldentey scored from the spot after Selina Cerci was tripped in the box.

The Gunners earlier thought they had scored when Chloe Kelly sent an outside-of-the-boot prod past Alberte Vingum, but her strike was ruled out after a VAR check deemed Stina Blackstenius to have been in an offside position and in the goalkeeper's eyeline.

But otherwise Arsenal looked toothless all too often, enjoying dominance of the ball but unable to find a way through.

The strength of the defensive performance from the visitors made a difference, too, with the energetic half-time celebrations of Koge boss Kristian Morch highlighting the determined nature of his side's display.

Arsenal lacked aggression in the final third and were often sloppy in possession, gifting opportunities for the Danish side to press and snatch the ball.

Gunners boss Renee Slegers had made eight changes from the side which salvaged a 1-1 draw with Manchester United at the weekend, but opted to switch things up at the break and introduce Alessia Russo in the place of Blackstenius in search of a goal threat.

But it provided little of the sort as the second half proceeded in the same manner as the first, with Arsenal dominating but struggling to fashion clear-cut chances.

They rescued it from the spot, however, as Vingum was unable to deny Caldentey from 12 yards despite managing to get a hand to her strike.

Analysis: Familiar frustrations as Arsenal struggle in front of goal

There was a clear sense of disappointment surrounding Arsenal going into this game, given their struggles in front of goal which played a large part in their 1-1 draw with Manchester United and stalemate with Crystal Palace.

Making eight changes following their United draw, in a week where they face Chelsea on Sunday (16:30 BST), was an understandable decision on Slegers' part.

However, as Arsenal's frustrations wore on throughout the game it only contributed to a feeling that they may not have afforded Koge the required respect.

The game progressed to a state where Arsenal seemingly prioritised quantity, not quality of chances as their decision-making continued to fall wide of the mark.

While they managed to find a way to win, it came only as a result of a piece of clumsy defending from Koge which gifted them the penalty.

Given the strength of opponents on the way for the Gunners in this competition, including a trip to the Nou Camp to face Barcelona and a game against European heavyweights Lyon, much improvement will need to be done.

articles.title: Colorado's Deion Sanders cuts players for 'conduct detrimental to the team'; S Ben Finneseth apologizes for jab at Northwestern
articles.summary: The Buffaloes are trying to hit the reset button following a 41-7 loss, before which Finneseth said Northwestern's temporary stadium "f***ing sucks."
articles.body:
Colorado 's Tuesday news conference began with a public apology from a sixth-year defender who went viral for disparaging Northwestern 's temporary stadium before the Buffaloes suffered a 41-7 loss to the Wildcats.

Later at the podium, head coach Deion Sanders revealed in the wake of that humbling defeat that he's removed players for "conduct detrimental to the team."

Sanders didn't mention those players by name or disclose how many of them were kicked off, but he emphasized that he no longer has a tolerance for selfish disposition.

When asked if those dismissals were the result of a pattern of behavior, Sanders explained that "it's never one [thing]."

"Those guys could tell you, I'm the most loving and giving and forgiving man you could ever meet, but when you start [doing] conduct detrimental to the team that will set us back and … you don't care about the team, you care about you — I have a problem with that.

"And a year ago, I didn't put my foot down in it enough. It lingered a little bit. Then it imploded. I'm not doing that. I'm not doing that anymore."

Colorado plummeted to 3-9 last season, a steep drop-off after it won nine games during the 2024 campaign, when Shedeur Sanders quarterbacked and two-way star Travis Hunter won the Heisman Trophy.

So far this time around, the Buffaloes are 2-1; however, they scored only 14 points in the first of those wins — a thrilling season opener against Georgia Tech — and blew out FCS Weber State to record the other.

Then they were boat raced by the Big Ten's Wildcats, right near Lake Michigan, off which 12,023 fans watched the beatdown at Northwestern Medicine Field at Martin Stadium. In the lead-up to that lopsided affair, Colorado safety Ben Finneseth was captured on video disparaging the stadium , which has housed Northwestern football during the construction of the new Ryan Field since the start of the 2024 season.

Finneseth, now in his sixth season with the Buffs, could be heard saying the temporary stadium "f***ing sucks" and "sounds like a f***ing library." His only snaps in the game came on special teams, per Pro Football Focus.

"I just wanted to apologize, first of all, to you guys, to everyone that's tied in with the university, to everyone at Northwestern, to everyone that supports us, to my teammates, to my coaches," Finneseth said Tuesday, standing next to Sanders while he delivered his statement.

"It was childish. It was a stupid thing that I said. It won't happen again. And the way I handled it was horrible. I promise you guys that it will not happen again, and it will be much more mature moving forward."

Northwestern faithful have reveled in the 34-point shellacking. David Braun's squad is 2-0 heading into Friday night's showdown with No. 5 Indiana in Bloomington.

The Wildcats will debut their new $862 million, 35,000-seat stadium stadium on Friday, Oct. 2, when they host Penn State .

"Coach Braun and Coach Kelly from Northwestern, I have the utmost respect [for them]," Sanders said in his opening statement, also referencing first-year Wildcats offensive coordinator Chip Kelly.

"Both of them came over to speak to me, and we had great conversations, and they went on to kick our butts, but I have the utmost respect for that school, that team, what they're doing with the program, and some foolishness came out of it, and we want to correct our wrongs and make it right right now."

Sanders additionally took issue with postgame shenanigans. In the immediate aftermath of the loss on Saturday, he vocalized disappointment in some of his players apparently treating the defeat as a "laughing matter."

Accountability was the theme of Sanders' Tuesday news conference. He's owning responsibility for his program's shortcomings, and he's requiring his players to do their part, too.

"We want to win. That's the No. 1 [priority], but we want to win the right way," said Sanders, a Pro Football Hall of Famer who is 18-22 in three-plus seasons at the helm of Colorado.

"We want to do what's right. But the whole thing is about winning. And we don't want to ever employ a losing type of sentiment. We don't want to do things that are associated with losers and bad-mouth opponents and do that kind of stuff. That's not who we are."

On-field discipline was an issue for the Buffs last week as well. They committed nine penalties and four turnovers.

"We are on everything right now with a microscope," Sanders said. "We're challenging them to be who they say they want to be."

Linebacker Tyler Martinez, a transfer from New Mexico State, admitted that the dismissals were hard to process, given how tight-knit the team is. But as a leader of the group, he also understands his coach's decision.

"The dismissals, it sucks in the moment, but when you look in the big picture, if it's going to help us win, we got to do it," Martinez said.

"And it is what it is. I'm sorry to see those guys go, but we have games to win here. So whatever it takes is whatever it takes.

articles.title: Juanma Castaño pide perdón pero mantiene su crítica a Real Madrid TV: "Miente, manipula, señala y hostiga"
articles.standfirst: El director de "El Partidazo" de la cadena COPE reconoce su error al compararla con el diario Gara
articles.summary: El director de "El Partidazo" de la cadena COPE reconoce su error al compararla con el diario Gara
articles.body: Juanma Castaño, director de "El Partidazo" de la cadena COPE, contestó al comunicado emitido por el Real Madrid este martes en relación a la columna del periodista en ABC en la que comparaba a Real Madrid TV con el diario Gara. El periodista asturiano reconoció su error y pidió perdón por su desafortunada comparación: "Es excesiva. Esta comparación sobra y pido perdón por por comparar a Real Madrid TV con el diario Gara. Pido disculpas por ello". Sin embargo, el locutor quiso dejar bien claro que su opinión sobre la televisión del club blanco sigue siendo la misma: "Mi opinión sobre Real Madrid TV es la misma que tengo en el resto del artículo y que tenía ayer y que tendré hasta que cambien su manera de actuar. Real Madrid TV miente, manipula, señala y hostiga", apuntó. El Real Madrid había emitido un comunicado horas antes en las que se defendía de esa comparación y atacaba con dureza al periodista, calificando su comparativa como "absolutamente deplorable e inadmisible". En su columna, titulada 'El Real Madrid, en guerra', Castaño escribió que "en la tele oficial, que es el diario Gara del ultraflorentinismo, piden abandonar las competiciones nacionales". La entidad blanca entiende que comparar su medio oficial con un periódico "cuya historia está vinculada al mundo de la banda terrorista ETA constituye un ejercicio extremadamente grave que traspasa todos los límites".

articles.title: LSU coach Lane Kiffin's return to Ole Miss draws nearly 11 million viewers
articles.summary: It's the second-most watched game of the 2026 season so far behind Texas' win over Ohio State.
articles.body:
The TV audience for Lane Kiffin's return to Ole Miss was sizable. But it also didn't come close to matching the viewership number for Texas' Week 2 win over Ohio State.

ESPN said Tuesday afternoon that Ole Miss' 32-24 win drew an average audience of 10.9 million viewers. It was by far the most-watched game of the day and the second game of the 2026 season to break the 10 million mark. Alabama's win over Florida State earlier in the day had 7 million watchers.

It was a certainty that the Rebels' victory would be the most-watched game of the weekend ever since the SEC announced its 2026 football schedule. Given the way that one of the most polarizing coaches in college football left Ole Miss at the end of the 2025 regular season for a hated rival and the fact that both teams are potential playoff contenders, it was always going to be one of the biggest games of the season.

The game delivered, too. After LSU scored 17 straight points to tie the game, Ole Miss retook the lead in the fourth quarter and sealed the game late with an interception in the end zone.

Yet Saturday night's game drew 3 million fewer viewers than Texas' 24-23 victory did. That game was ESPN's most-watched regular-season game since Ohio State played Michigan on ABC in 2016.

If you want to make a sweeping judgment about the viewership numbers, it's reasonable to think that brand power is still one of the biggest driving forces in college football viewership. While Kiffin has been the central figure of the 2026 offseason, the fascination with him was still trumped by the wide appeal — and population advantage — of schools like Ohio State and Texas.

articles.title: El último testigo del juicio no descarta que Maradona muriera por covid
articles.standfirst: Pablo Ferrari habla de "error metodológico"
articles.summary: Pablo Ferrari habla de "error metodológico"
articles.body: El perito oficial Pablo Ferrari, último testigo del juicio por la muerte de Maradona, dijo ante el tribunal que no puede descartar que Diego muriera a causa de covid-19. "No podemos descartar que haya muerto de covid", dijo Ferrari, al señalar que fue "un error metodológico" no haberle realizado una prueba de detección del coronavirus como parte de la autopsia. Maradona murió el 25 de noviembre de 2020, en plena pandemia de covid-19, mientras recibía tratamiento domiciliario en una casa de las afueras de Buenos Aires. "La enfermedad del coronavirus ingresaba por las vías respiratorias y podía ser fulminante en su virulencia y matar al paciente en pocas horas", señaló Ferrari, médico forense, pediatra y perito oficial de la Justicia. El último testigo del juicio, que comenzó el 14 de abril pasado en los tribunales de la localidad de San Isidro, causó sorpresa al plantear una hipótesis que no había sido mencionada en 43 audiencias previas, por las que desfilaron 76 testigos. Ferrari participó en una pericia solicitada en 2025 por la defensa del principal acusado, Leopoldo Luque. Según el perito oficial, Maradona acumuló líquido en el pulmón durante un período de tiempo corto, que podía ser minutos o pocas horas, y eso provocó un ahogamiento que derivó en un paro cardíaco. Mientras otros peritos oficiales afirmaron al comienzo del juicio que Maradona tuvo una agonía que pudo haberse extendido durante 12 horas, Ferrari afirmó: "Tuvo que haber sido de pocos minutos su agonía". Peritos convocados por los acusados declararon previamente que la muerte de Maradona fue repentina, pero Ferrari es el único perito oficial en sostener esta visión de los hechos, por lo que resulta un testigo clave para la defensa de Luque, señalado a lo largo del juicio como el médico a cargo de la salud del exfutbolista. La próxima audiencia se celebrará el 29 de septiembre, fecha en que los acusados comenzarán a ampliar sus declaraciones. Está previsto que los alegatos comiencen el 6 de octubre y que el juicio se extienda hasta finales de ese mes. Además de a Luque, se juzga en este proceso a la psiquiatra Agustina Cosachov, la coordinadora de cuidados domiciliarios de Swiss Medical, Nancy Forlini, el psicólogo Carlos Díaz, el coordinador de enfermeros Mariano Perroni, el enfermero Ricardo Almirón y el médico clínico Pedro Di Spagna, todos acusados de homicidio simple con dolo eventual.
